topic: Benjamin Franklin calming waves with oil
script: Benjamin Franklin calmed a windy pond with almost no oil. Clapham Common pond heaves under gusts and whitecaps. Franklin grips a small vial at the bank. A sea captain watches, shakes his head, and walks off. Can a teaspoon of oil quiet a pond? Franklin pours a quick splash at the edge. It spreads, but the chop rolls straight through. The wind climbs and roughens the surface. Benjamin Franklin studies the gusts, then shifts a few steps upwind. He drips a slow, steady thread into the breeze. The thin slick rides the surface downwind. One drop blossoms into a wide rainbow sheen. Why do ripples fade? The film weakens surface pull and kills tiny waves. Bigger swells still move under; crests soften. Then he tries it from a ship near Portsmouth. A glassy lane forms and the spray falls. Franklin writes the Royal Society in 1774 about acres smoothed. Small ripples stop; oil makes them vanish. A windy pond shows a smooth path growing wider.
